# Power Ledger — THE CONDITION REPORT

One row per chapter in which the power relationship is in play, in chapter
order. Darker lead: Sebastiaan Corvelijn. Constrained lead: Lena Brassart.
Everyone named here appears in `characters.md`.

| # | Chapter | Who holds the power, and what makes it real | What the darker lead does with it | What the other lead does about it | Which way the balance moves | What cannot be taken back |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ch_03 | Lena — she is a free contractor and he needs a registered signature Zurich will accept | hires her; keeps his coat on; does not enter the room | signs one genuine condition report on the Feininger, freely | to her, slightly — he needs something only she can give | her real signature exists on file, and he now has a specimen of her hand |
| 2 | ch_04 | Sebastiaan — a Rotring, her staff card, a public register number, and a paid clerk | forges her signature onto a 40-page report and files it; pays Bram Six for a same-day stamp | nothing; she is upstairs | to him, hard, and irreversibly | the filing is on the docket under Article 11 and can never be removed |
| 3 | ch_05 | Sebastiaan — the filed document, plus the 1997 report in his drawer | produces the 1997 report unasked and lays it on the table like a valuation | goes to Brussels alone, questions Rachida, declines to answer Rachida's question about authorship | to him — she now knows the exits and their prices | Rachida has seen her decline to disown the signature; that non-answer is on the record between them |
| 4 | ch_06 | Sebastiaan — the house, the schedule, the keys | sets the working arrangement; gives her the alarm code 1109 | accepts the arrangement and takes the code | to him, and it costs him nothing yet | she can leave the building at night without asking, which he can never un-tell her |
| 5 | ch_07 | Sebastiaan — but a mechanism has become visible | nothing; he does not know she is in Brussels | prices every exit with Vervoort and writes down what a corrigendum is | level, briefly — she gains the knowledge that will end the book | she knows the one instrument that can undo him, and he does not know she knows |

| 7 | ch_10 | Sebastiaan — over third parties, not over her | does **nothing** to override her; instead tells Kasimir Ott to make Tomas Beke unavailable | is not present; the decision is taken about someone else | to him in the world, unmoved between them | Beke's arrest is set in motion; Sebastiaan has said "do it" out loud |

| 10 | ch_14 | Sebastiaan — quietly, by substitution | lets her burn a laser print and keeps the original in the strongroom | burns it and believes it | to him, secretly — the ledger records a move she does not know about | the deception exists and is physical: a paperclip rust-mark on a sheet in the strongroom |

| 12 | ch_18 | Lena, unknowingly | dismisses Kasimir's warning that she has a key, a grudge and a set of hands | keeps working and says nothing | unmoved, and the stillness is the point | Kasimir has now said it out loud once and will remember that he did |
| 13 | ch_19 | level — the only genuinely level chapter in the book | crosses the doorframe for the first time in six weeks, on stated terms | **sets the terms and names the word that ends it: "Basel"** | level — each now has something to lose that is not the other's compliance | there is an agreed limit and a spoken word, and afterwards both of them said what it was |
| 14 | ch_20 | Sebastiaan — collateral, kept | defends keeping the original as rational, and becomes more accurate as he lies | finds the absence of the rust-mark inside four seconds; names his tell aloud; does not leave | to him in fact, to her in standing | she will not believe an object he hands her again |

| 25 | ch_32 | Lena — over her own account of events | not present | **writes out what she did on 22 February and decides to file it herself, before anyone asks** | to her — she takes her own case out of everyone's hands | she has chosen the visible repair; the decision precedes anything he does |

| 29 | ch_38 | Lena — she has no tie, no debt, no leverage on her, and a bench held open in Rotterdam | asks a direct question and waits for the answer | **chooses to stay, and states that the reason is not what he gave up** | to her, finally and permanently | she has chosen with the door open; her hand will not steady; the fellowship is gone |

---

- **The balance first moves toward the constrained lead** at **ch_09**, which
  is **23.7%** of the book — her refusal of the Feininger signature, which is
  never overridden and stalls the claim for fourteen chapters.
- **The darker lead's largest cost** falls at **ch_33**, which is **86.8%** —
  the corrigendum naming himself as the forger and the clause 9 resignation
  of the stewardship into Commission escrow, with the five-year bar arriving
  as its direct consequence at ch_35 (92.1%).
- **Do any three consecutive rows leave the balance unmoved?** No. The
  longest unmoved run is one row (rows 12, 24 and 28 in isolation), and each
  is immediately followed by a move. Rows 12 and 24 are deliberate stillness
  before a hinge; row 28 is the only row in the book where a great deal
  happens in the world and nothing at all happens between them.

### Cross-checks against the outline

- **Actions rather than endurance in the constrained lead's column:** rows
  6, 9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 21, 23, 25, 29 — ten. Row 18 is the only chapter in
  which she is physically held, and it still contains three actions.
- **Which of her actions changes what a later row can contain:** row 6
  (ch_09) forecloses a second forged signature and makes rows 15 and 22
  possible; row 11 (ch_17) creates the object that rows 22 and 26 both turn
  on; row 16 (ch_23) fires the audit right that produces rows 17, 18 and 22;
  row 25 (ch_32) means row 26's outcome is not his to give her.
- **A cost to the darker lead in the world's own currency before the 90%
  mark:** row 26 (ch_33, 86.8%) — the stewardship, the claim book, and a
  signed confession to a regulator with referral powers. Earlier and
  smaller: row 7 (ch_10), where declining to override her costs him the
  March window; row 20 (ch_27), where the missed reckoning costs him five
  points of interest and the audit deadline.
- **`What cannot be taken back` referred back to later:** row 2's filing is
  referred to in ch_05, ch_20, ch_29 and ch_33. Row 6's stalled claim runs
  through ch_10, ch_22 and ch_27. Row 11's receipt detonates in ch_29 and is
  disclosed in ch_32. Row 18's tremor is present in ch_28, ch_32, ch_34,
  ch_36 and ch_38. Row 8's Beke is still unrestored in ch_36.
- **The final row could not have been the first:** row 29 depends on row 26
  (the hold had to be ended by his decision before her choice could mean
  anything), on row 25 (she had already chosen her own account independently
  of him), and on row 18 (she is choosing with a hand that will not steady,
  which is what makes the choice cost something).
